national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said India needs a strong and integrated maritime ecosystem to further enhance its maritime power and strengthen the country’s defence capabilities. The Defence Minister today launched Fleet Support Ship-1, laid the keel for Fleet Support Ship-5 and inaugurated the upgraded Slipway-4 and a 300-tonne Goliath Crane at Hindustan Shipyard Limited in Visakhapatnam. Addressing the gathering, Mr Singh said the launch of Fleet Support Ship-1, keel laying of Fleet Support Ship-5 and inauguration of upgraded infrastructure at HSL mark important steps in strengthening India’s maritime capabilities. He said Fleet Support Ship-1, named ‘Surya’, will strengthen the Indian Navy’s reach, endurance and operational effectiveness. He said the new slipway and Goliath crane at HSL will further enhance the shipyard’s capacity to undertake large shipbuilding projects. The Defence Minister said the Indian Navy has repeatedly demonstrated its capabilities in the Indian Ocean Region as a first responder and preferred security partner. He said the Navy has played an important role in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, anti-piracy operations, evacuation missions and maritime security. Mr Singh said, Hindustan Shipyard Limited has played an important role in meeting India’s maritime and defence requirements for more than eight decades. He said the shipyard’s Miniratna Category-I status, accorded in 2025, reflects its transformation and improved financial position. The Defence Minister said the Navy, shipyards, DRDO, academia, industry, MSMEs and start-ups need to work together as an integrated team to build a strong national maritime ecosystem. Mr Singh said India has immense potential in shipbuilding, but the challenge is to convert this potential into capability and global competitiveness. He stressed the need to focus on timely delivery, productivity, indigenous design capability, resilient supply chains, skilled manpower, capacity expansion and cost competitiveness. He said India’s defence manufacturing sector has undergone significant transformation over the past decade, with the country moving from dependence on imported platforms towards designing and manufacturing advanced systems and platforms domestically. Mr Singh said India aims to become a developed nation by 2047, with a self-reliant, secure and prosperous economy and a respected position in the world.

national_raw_news.content: India’s National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore teleconsultations, marking a significant milestone in the Government’s efforts to leverage digital technology to make quality healthcare more accessible, affordable and equitable for citizens across the country. The platform recorded over 50 crore teleconsultations cumulatively across all States and Union Territories. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare said that the achievement reflects the growing role of telemedicine in complementing the country’s existing healthcare delivery system and in overcoming barriers of distance, geography and access, particularly for citizens living in rural, remote and underserved areas. eSanjeevani has emerged as an important component of the country’s digital health ecosystem and as the world’s largest telemedicine implementation in primary healthcare. Further, the platform has extended the reach of public healthcare services beyond the physical boundaries of conventional health facilities and brought medical consultations closer to people in the communities where they live. The service has witnessed rapid and sustained expansion since its inception. The initiative currently supports more than 1.42 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir spokes, over 19 thousand medical hubs and 901 online OPDs, with over two lakh registered healthcare providers. The platform is facilitating around 2.5 to 3 lakh consultations every day in 15 languages, including English and 14 Indian languages. Its highest single-day utilisation has crossed six lakh consultations. Women account for over 57 per cent of total utilisation, while 40 per cent of consultations are availed by citizens aged 46 years and above, including 16.25 per cent by senior citizens aged 60 years and above. The platform has evolved with the integration of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Clinical Decision Support System (AI-CDSS), which supports healthcare providers during consultations and assists in strengthening the quality, consistency and efficiency of clinical decision-making. The innovation has received national recognition with the Gold Award under the National Awards for e-Governance 2026. eSanjeevani has also been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System-112, enabling stronger linkages between emergency response services and remote medical expertise. The integration is aimed at facilitating more coordinated access to medical support and further strengthening the use of digital technology in emergency healthcare. eSanjeevani is now expanding to facilitate specialist OPD consultations through premier government medical institutions. Patient-to-doctor teleconsultation services for select specialities have been rolled out at AIIMS Jodhpur, AIIMS Jammu and AIIMS Patna. eSanjeevani is a Made-in-India digital health solution developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), with C-DAC Mohali providing end-to-end technological development and engineering support since its inception. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has played a central role in guiding the continuous evolution of the platform in response to the emerging needs of India’s healthcare system.
